newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover up in week to May 23.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover up in week to May 23.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Monday a 29.14 percent rise in its turnover during the week ending May 23 on an improved market liqudity.
Total turnover rose to 65.091 million dinars ($11.63 million) from 50.403 million a week ago, while the number of transactions fell to 183 from 196.
While the primary market activity declined to 39.827 million dinars from 49.838 million a week ago, the secondary market surged to 25.264 million dinars from 0.565 million.
Traders said market liquidity has been improving since the beginning of the year but not due to expanding money supply.

"The central bank is not printing new money. But there is simply no economic activity in this country and those who have some money place it on the bourse to earn on high interest," a trader told Reuters.
For the week ending May 23, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper traded 168 times for a volume of 25.598 million dinars.
* Treasury bills accounted for seven transactions totalling 1.229 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between a monthly 7.00 and 16.76 percent, while maturity stood between six and 30 days.
* No state treasury-bills were sold during the week, the bourse said.
* Central bank short-term bonds traded three times for a total 13.0 million dinars.
* The central bank continued to sell bonds from its bond portfolio on the secondary market. The NBY sold 25.264 million dinars worth of bonds issued by the Serbian Commodity Reserve Agency.
* Over-the-counter trade in commercial paper and treasury bills rose to 37.541 million dinars from 31 million a week ago.
* OTC trade in giro-money, where banks trade their surplus liquidity surged to 30.525 million dinars from 16.7 million a week ago.
